# Introduction and Overview

In this assignment, the New York Times (NYT) Application Programming Interface (API) will be accessed. Data from at least two endpoints will be collected in R. The JSON responses will be parsed into data frames, which will then be tidied and analyzed. One potential avenue of investigation is quantifying the prevalence of "AI", "LLM", and other keywords in the NYT historical records. To accomplish this, the following endpoints will be accessed:

1.  Books API

    - This API provides data about books on the NYT Best Sellers lists. This can help determine the relevant prevalence of AI-focused books in the NYT lists.

2.  Archive API

    - This API provides data about articles for a given month, extending back to 1851. This can be used to develop a deep historical viewpoint on the rise of these keywords in popular media.

Anticipated challenges include safe secret storage, scoping the data pulls to limit file size, and comparing data from books to articles.

# Approach

1.  Sign up for NYT API credentials

    1.  <https://developer.nytimes.com/>

2.  Save access keys and secrets to local `.Renviron` file.

    1.  This avoids leaking secrets and keeps them local

3.  Probe the API endpoints with test scripts

    1.  Confirm connection is successful and shape of queried data matches expectations

4.  Ingest API data and parse into data frames.

    1.  Optional challenge: store data in parquet files (arrow package)

5.  Tidy data frames and prepare for downstream analysis

# Codebase

## API Access Testing

```{r load-packages}
#|echo: FALSE
#|warning: FALSE
#|message: FALSE

library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)
library(arrow)

```

```{r test-books}
#|echo: TRUE
#|warning: FALSE
#|message: FALSE

if (Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY") == "") {
  stop("NYT_API_KEY not found in environment. Please set in .Renviron file.")
}

if (Sys.getenv("NYT_API_SECRET") == "") {
  stop("NYT_SECRET_KEY not found in environment. Please set in .Renviron file.")
}

books_url <- "https://api.nytimes.com/svc/books/v3/lists/full-overview.json"

req <- request(books_url) |>        # Structures request object with credentials
  req_url_query(`api-key` = Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY"),
                `secret-key` = Sys.getenv("NYT_API_SECRET"))

resp <- req_perform(req)            # Loads response from request

stopifnot(resp_status(resp) == 200) # Stops if HTTP status is not 200 OK

raw_json <- resp |>                 # Parse JSON data into raw frame
  resp_body_string() |> 
  fromJSON(flatten = TRUE)

names(raw_json)
# Print status code
raw_json$status 

# Print number of results in JSON object
raw_json$num_results

books_df <- as_tibble(raw_json$results$lists) |>
  unnest(books)

knitr::kable(head(books_df[,12:13]))


```

```{r test-archive}
#|echo: TRUE
#|warning: FALSE
#|message: FALSE

if (Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY") == "") {
  stop("NYT_API_KEY not found in environment. Please set in .Renviron file.")
}

if (Sys.getenv("NYT_API_SECRET") == "") {
  stop("NYT_SECRET_KEY not found in environment. Please set in .Renviron file.")
}

archive_url <- "https://api.nytimes.com/svc/archive/v1/2026/1.json"

req2 <- request(archive_url) |>        # Structures request object with credentials
  req_url_query(`api-key` = Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY"),
                `secret-key` = Sys.getenv("NYT_API_SECRET"))

resp2 <- req_perform(req2)            # Loads response from request

stopifnot(resp_status(resp2) == 200) # Stops if HTTP status is not 200 OK

raw_json2 <- resp2 |>                 # Parse JSON data into raw frame
  resp_body_string() |> 
  fromJSON(flatten = TRUE)

# check structure of raw json
names(raw_json2)
names(raw_json2$response)
names(raw_json2$response$meta)

# Print number of results in JSON object
raw_json2$response$meta$hits

archive_df <- as_tibble(raw_json2$response$docs)
  
knitr::kable(head(archive_df[,1:3],3))

```

Both tests passed (`status = 200` and real data in glimpses), so now data can be ingested and tidied to prepare for analysis.

## Ingesting API data

### Saving archive data into parquet files

```{r}

parquet_path <- "nyt_archive_2026_01.parquet"

if(!file.exists(parquet_path)){
  resp2 <- request(archive_url) |>
    req_url_query(`api-key` = Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY"),
                  `secret-key` = Sys.getenv("NYT_API_SECRET")) |> 
    req_perform()
  
  stopifnot(resp_status(resp2) == 200)
  
}
```
